listings.name: Jacob Ten Broeck House (HGTV 'Would You Buy This Haunted House?' Kingston stop - match unconfirmed)
listings.summary: c.1773 stone Federal landmark; HGTV's Oct 2026 episode toured a 1773 Kingston mansion 'said to be home to lingering spirits'

images.caption: Illustration of Jacob Ten Broeck House (HGTV 'Would You Buy This Haunted House?' Kingston stop - match unconfirmed) (not a photo)
images.credit: Illustration by Twisted Deeds (not a photo)

listings.name: Old Henrico County Courthouse & Jail
listings.summary: 1896 courthouse, sheriff's office and jail on the site that was Henrico's county seat from 1752; three levels of jail cells remain

listings.name: Fossores Chapter House (Hugh H. Richard House)
listings.summary: 1888 Queen Anne run as a 'gravedigger' ministry retreat with 'macabre' Gothic decor; Airbnb renters trashed it in 2022

images.author: Andrew Jameson
images.caption: Hugh H Richard House Jackson MI
images.credit: Andrew Jameson, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

listings.name: Former funeral home, New Florence
listings.summary: 1958 building that 'has operated as a funeral home since its construction'; the sale bars the buyer from running a funeral home or crematory for 30 years

listings.name: Judge Oliver house (Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil link)
listings.summary: Once owned by the judge who presided over the Jim Williams murder trial ('Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil')

listings.name: Brownsville Road House ('The Demon of Brownsville Road')
listings.price: $625,000 asking (as operating B&B; also offered as a single-family home at $550,000)
listings.summary: An 1899 Brentwood Victorian, now a B&B, at the center of a former county commissioner's published account of a demonic haunting and exorcism.
listings.facts: 6 guest bd · 4 ba · 4,444 sqft · 0.46 ac · built 1899
listings.loreTeaser: The owner says the house was exorcised years ago, and the sale discloses the story. Accounts of what happened there are the family's own claims.

listings.name: Wheeler Mansion (former Eastern Star Home)
listings.summary: A 1903 sewing-machine fortune mansion where its builder died in 1910, later a rest home for 65 years, then foreclosed and left to rot before a full restoration.
listings.loreTeaser: Local lore says John W. Wheeler and the Eastern Star ladies never left; the current owner calls them 'prankster-ish'. The hedge maze is real.

images.caption: Illustration of Wheeler Mansion (former Eastern Star Home) (not a photo)
images.credit: Illustration by Twisted Deeds (not a photo)

listings.name: The Haunted Hotel (623 Ursulines, French Quarter)
listings.summary: An 1829 French Quarter hotel that sells itself as the city's oldest haunted hotel, with 19 themed rooms and its own Axeman legend.
listings.loreTeaser: Hotel lore says the Axeman rented a back room and that renovators found an axe, which is now displayed in the lobby. Treat it as legend: the killer was never…

listings.name: Lumber Baron Inn (John Mouat House)
listings.summary: An 1890 lumber-baron mansion, now a B&B, where an unsolved 1970 double homicide happened while it was apartments; it is for sale with its ballroom intact.
listings.loreTeaser: Guests most often report activity in one former apartment. The 1970 case was never solved, so the story is told with care.

listings.name: Castle Rock (roadside lookout & Paul Bunyan statues)
listings.address: N2690 Castle Rock Rd, St. Ignace, MI 49781
listings.summary: A 195-foot limestone sea stack north of the Mackinac Bridge that has been sold to tourists since 1929 as an ancient Ojibwe lookout, a claim historians say probably belongs to nearby Rabbit's Back.
listings.loreTeaser: Lore: Promotional Indigenous lookout legend ('Pontiac's/Ojibway lookout', disputed) + Paul Bunyan tall-tale statues
listings.geo_source: Twisted Deeds map layer (landmark (Nominatim, Castle Rock))

listings.name: Guntown Mountain (former Wild West theme park)
listings.address: 101 Huckleberry Knob Rd, Cave City, KY 42127
listings.summary: A Wild West town on a hilltop over I-65, reached by a 1969 chairlift, with staged gunfights, can-can shows and a Haunted Hotel walk-through.
listings.loreTeaser: It closed in 2013, reopened for one chaotic 2015 summer as 'Funtown Mountain' until the city shut it over code violations, was sold at auction in 2016, came…

listings.name: Eppstein House (Frank Lloyd Wright Usonian, The Acres)
listings.summary: A 1953 Frank Lloyd Wright Usonian house in 'The Acres', a cooperative colony of Upjohn scientists.
listings.loreTeaser: They bought farmland in 1947 for 21 circular one-acre lots, and only four Wright houses were ever built.

listings.name: Earl Young's Thatch House (Young's first house)
listings.summary: This was the first house of Earl Young, the self-taught builder behind Charlevoix's storybook 'mushroom houses'.
listings.loreTeaser: He began it in 1918 using boulders gathered around Lake Michigan and his family lived there into the late 1940s.

listings.name: Zinc Collar Pad Company Building
listings.summary: An 1875 Italianate factory built after fire destroyed the first plant.
listings.loreTeaser: It made Dexter Curtis's patented zinc-lined horse-collar pads, which sold nationwide, became apartments after the company left in 1913, and has stood empty…

listings.name: Former Pirate's Park (closed fun park, Flint Township)
listings.summary: A pirate-themed fun park that opened in 1991 with mini golf, go-karts and a 420-foot water slide.
listings.loreTeaser: It closed in 2011 and decayed for years while reopening plans fell through, then was demolished in June 2024.

listings.name: Skillagalee (Ile aux Galets) + Gravelly Shoal Lighthouses (two-light package)
listings.summary: Two Great Lakes lighthouses for less than a starter home.
listings.loreTeaser: One is the 1888 brick tower on Ile aux Galets, the 'island of pebbles' 7 miles off Cross Village; the other is the 1939-41 Art Deco Gravelly Shoal light in…
listings.geo_source: Twisted Deeds map layer (landmark (Nominatim, Ile aux Galets island); Gravelly Shoal light is a second site in Saginaw Bay)

listings.name: Middle Island & Lighthouse (227-acre Lake Huron island)
listings.summary: A 227-acre island in the Thunder Bay shipwreck graveyard, with a 76-foot lighthouse first lit in 1905.
listings.loreTeaser: Volunteer keepers spent decades restoring the station from 1992 and turned its fog-signal building into a remote overnight inn.
listings.geo_source: Twisted Deeds map layer (landmark (Nominatim, Middle Island Light))

listings.name: Farrand Hall (1854 Greek Revival homestead)
listings.summary: A pioneer's 1854 Greek Revival mansion with a 170-year chain of ownership on the record.
listings.loreTeaser: Henry K. Farrand arrived in 1836 and his wife died the year after the house was finished.

listings.name: Former Moline Public Library (1904 Carnegie)
listings.summary: A Neoclassical Carnegie library that opened in 1904 with Ionic columns and five fireplaces.
listings.loreTeaser: It closed as a library in 2009 and stood empty until a music conservatory moved in in 2023.

listings.name: Former Kendallville Carnegie Library
listings.summary: Kendallville's Carnegie library (cornerstone 1913, finished 1914) served the town until 1968.
listings.loreTeaser: It then passed through a law firm, an architecture practice, a vintage shop and an art gallery, and is now going to online auction with a published minimum bid.

images.caption: Illustration of Former Kendallville Carnegie Library (not a photo)
images.credit: Illustration by Twisted Deeds (not a photo)

listings.name: Former Fantasy Island amusement park (Silver Comet coaster)
listings.address: 2400 Grand Island Blvd, Grand Island, NY 14072
listings.summary: A 1961 Western New York amusement park, rides and Wild West town still standing, that did not open in 2026 and is now for sale whole.
listings.loreTeaser: The sale includes the Silver Comet wooden coaster, a water park, Kiddie Land and the old Western Town stage.

images.author: anthony dyer
images.caption: Silver comet station
images.credit: anthony dyer, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

listings.name: Old Pearce Mercantile (Pearce General Store), Pearce ghost town
listings.address: 905 S Ghost Town Trl, Pearce, AZ 85625
listings.summary: The tallest adobe building in Cochise County: the 1890s general store of the Pearce gold-mining boomtown, now a ghost town, restored and for sale.
listings.loreTeaser: The store served as Pearce's bank and post office while the Commonwealth Mine boomed, and it stayed open long after the town emptied.

images.author: Marine 69-71
images.caption: Pearce-Building-Pearce General Store-1896
images.credit: Marine 69-71, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

listings.name: Frisco-Bagley Mill (near Animas Forks ghost town)
listings.place: Animas Forks area, San Juan, CO
listings.summary: A 1912 gold-mining mill standing at timberline just past the Animas Forks ghost town, National Register-listed, for sale with 31 acres.
listings.facts: 1 bd cabin · 300 sqft · 30.99 ac · mill built 1912
listings.loreTeaser: The mill was built from pre-cut, code-marked timbers in Silverton and assembled on the mountainside.

listings.name: Verdier Mansion ('House of the Grand Passion')
listings.place: San Francisco (Russian Hill), San Francisco, CA
listings.summary: A 1906 Russian Hill mansion that has been, by most accounts, an heir's home, an opium den, Sally Stanford's brothel and a wartime officers' club.
listings.facts: 6 bd · 6 full + 2 half ba · 9,545 sqft · 8,285 sf lot · built 1906-07
listings.loreTeaser: Squatters are said to have come in through tunnels underneath. The madam who ran the house later became mayor of Sausalito.

listings.name: Brook Forest Inn
listings.address: 8136 S Brook Forest Rd, Evergreen, CO 80439
listings.summary: A National Register Swiss-chalet inn in the foothills with a century of guests and an enduring ghost legend about a stable hand named Carl.
listings.facts: 16 guest rooms · 15,907 sqft · 2.5 acres · built 1909 (inn 1919) · NRHP
listings.loreTeaser: Its third floor was reportedly sealed off at one time. Legend says Carl never checked out.

images.caption: Illustration of Brook Forest Inn (not a photo)
images.credit: Illustration by Twisted Deeds (not a photo)

listings.name: Former Jackson County Detention Center block
listings.address: 1300 Cherry St (block bounded by Locust, Cherry, 13th & 14th Sts), Kansas City, MO 64106
listings.summary: Kansas City's emptied downtown county jail, once the subject of a damning grand-jury report, is for sale by sealed bid along with its whole block.
listings.facts: Near-full downtown city block; former detention center plus several county buildings; county says demolish or reuse
listings.loreTeaser: The county's own executive says it is 'nothing we can renovate.' Bids close the week of Thanksgiving.

listings.name: Pete's Tavern Building
listings.summary: A small downtown Nampa building with a reported past as a brothel and a speakeasy, a tavern since 1945, and a local ghost reputation.
listings.facts: 3,080 SF mixed-use retail building with basement and upstairs apartment; built c.1889-1907
listings.loreTeaser: Butcher, laundry, brothel and speakeasy, by most accounts, then a bar since 1945. Some say not every regular left.

listings.name: Belden Town (entire Gold Rush settlement)
listings.place: Feather River Canyon, Plumas County, CA
listings.summary: A whole Gold Rush-era settlement in the Feather River Canyon, saloon and schoolhouse included, is for sale as a single property.
listings.facts: ~4 acres riverfront · 18 hotel rooms · 7 cabins · 16 RV spaces · restaurant+bar (Type 47) · general store · ~20,007 SF hospitality space
listings.loreTeaser: Population about 15. The sale ads say you can 'be your own mayor'; legally, you can't.

images.caption: Illustration of Belden Town (entire Gold Rush settlement) (not a photo)
images.credit: Illustration by Twisted Deeds (not a photo)
